newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL says 13.5pct gas price hike not enough.
newsitem.headline: MOL says 13.5pct gas price hike not enough.

text.p: Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt said on Monday a 13.5 percent wholesale gas price rise from July 1 would not give the company the eight percent return on equity it is entitled to.
The wholesale price is the price that MOL pays for its gas supplies, which come mostly from Russia.
"We would have needed a higher gas price increase in order to bring our gas business out of the red and give an eight percent return," MOL CEO Zoltan Mandoki told journalists on Monday.
Hungary's Energy Office announced earlier today a 13.5 percent gas wholesale price increase as of July 1.

Hungary's energy law stipulates that energy companies are entitled to recover their expenses and should have a profit margin on their sales while a separate ministerial decree sets this margin at eight percent of their equity.
Since January, the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism revises gas and electricity prices quarterly according to a price formula incorporating justified production or supply costs.
Mandoki said that an eight percent return on equity would mean some eight billion forints of profits per year for MOL's gas business.
Mandoki added that last year MOL's gas business was 12.6 billion forints in the red while in the first half of 1997 the loss would be around seven billion forints.
Last year MOL sold 12.4 billion cubic meters of natural gas, of which 8.9 billion cubic meters were imported, mostly from Russia.
MOL has bought the gas at near world market prices and sold it in Hungary at state-controlled prices resulting in an average loss of 2.54 forints per cubic meter.

Mandoki could not say whether the current price increase would bring MOL's gas business out of the red but said the company asked the government to lower or abolish a five percent customs administration fee on its gas imports.
"We did propose this (abolition) to the government, but that was a separate development, independent of the gas price increase," Mandoki said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, MOL shares closed at 4,040 forints, down 40.
